verdictVocabulary.pass: meets the rule as rendered, no caveats
verdictVocabulary.fixable: misses the rule but the fix is known and cheap -- note MUST say what
verdictVocabulary.fail: misses the rule, ships broken if unaddressed
verdictVocabulary.unreviewed: not yet judged by a human or fresh-context agent -- the template default

items.rule: If a reference figure is being followed: which stage is this -- REPRODUCE (faithful copy), REPAIR (fix what the reference does badly), or ADAPT (this paper's own figure)? A stage-1 reproduction must NOT ship; an adaptation must not still be a copy.
items.note: ADAPT: this is the thesis-specific training-only architecture, not a reproduction.

items.rule: Pure-black #000000 text on a white canvas. Fills are a LAYERED system -- white, light gray, or a semantic tint are all correct; a grouping may also be a borderless tint field, a dashed boundary, or a gray wedge backplate.
items.note: Reviewed on the current color and grayscale rasters.

items.rule: Each hue holds a STABLE ROLE (not one global meaning): saturated/gray = active/inactive, warm tint = the special or selected subsystem, red = the exceptional structural accent ONLY. Ordinary outlines and routine connectors stay black/gray; fills may carry the semantic roles.
items.note: Blue identifies Main and warm brown identifies Catfish/shaping; labels and topology reinforce both roles.

items.rule: No gradient/shadow/glow/3D/photo texture. Flat semantic pictograms ARE the vocabulary and are encouraged. Corners modestly rounded but still read as rectangles -- never a pill or a glassy bubble.

Structural card outlines and ordinary process connectors use 1-2 weights; pictograms, wireless marks and legend swatches carry their own geometry and are OUTSIDE that budget. Emphasis = a thicker stroke or the accent colour, never a dark fill.
items.note: Structural and directional strokes remain visually distinct.

items.rule: One serif family (Times-like) matching the paper body; roughly 3-4 restrained size levels (a dense overview may use more); ONE idea per card; vertical labels are whole words rotated, never letter-stacked.
items.note: Times-like serif is consistent; variable symbols remain italic while ordinary words remain roman.

items.rule: Stable meaningful pictograms -- the same icon means the same entity every time, and MORE THAN ONE recurring identity glyph is normal. Recurring pictograms need no legend; a non-self-evident colour/link encoding earns a compact FRAMELESS key; a one-off icon must be labelled.
items.note: The satellite and circular-beam glyphs recur with the same meaning in both training loops.

items.rule: Judge by figure TYPE: a mechanism-detail figure is spacious with large text; a system/overview figure is legitimately VERY dense and must NOT be cleaned up into airy uniformity. The invariant is concise local text + explicit grouping + readable separation of the major flows.
items.note: Dense by design, while the Main and Catfish loops retain separate labelled bands and readable local modules.

items.rule: Self-evident spine (or row-major fold). Semantic panel HEADINGS are allowed -- framed, bold on a tint field, or floated beside a stage; what is banned is a detached narrative title or caption sentence. The three observed dashed roles (grouping / spatial region / comparison level) need no legend.
items.note: Each loop reads state to Q heads to scalarization to action selection to rollout, buffer, and TD update.

items.rule: No explanatory SENTENCES or paragraphs on the canvas -- short descriptive fragments and noun phrases are normal and expected. The test is: does it NARRATE? A fragment names a thing; a sentence explains it.
items.note: Canvas text is concise module or route terminology, not explanatory prose.

items.rule: Symbols and short words label the MAJOR units. Compact maths is allowed in six classes only (symbol/function label, parameter value, branch condition, bookkeeping update, ratio, count/coordinate/unit). A DEFINING equation or a decomposition of a research quantity NEVER appears -- it belongs in the caption.
items.note: Only compact state, Q-head, reward, and loss symbols appear.

items.rule: Whole-canvas balance at print scale: no dead zones / empty regions left once every box individually passes rule 7.
items.note: The lower shaping band fills the supporting space without obscuring either core training loop.

items.rule: At a glance the eye actually follows the intended flow -- the holistic read, not just the structural self-evidence rule 8 encodes.
items.note: The two horizontal loops are read first; the only cross-loop flows originate from the explicit shaping band.

items.rule: Every edge label is unambiguous about which arrow it names -- no near-miss with a neighboring edge or label.
items.note: The concise lower modules use unambiguous orthogonal arrows; no edge label competes with another route.

items.rule: Every semantic distinction (hue-encoded meaning, dashed-vs-solid, emphasis stroke) still reads once the figure is converted to grayscale.
items.note: The grayscale raster remains legible because Main/Catfish are also separated by band headings, labels, and route topology.
